issues.description: Ben says he has rented a flat (s1l1), but then says 'The house has a big room.' A flat is not a house, and the switch may confuse learners and contradicts the on-screen story.
issues.suggested_fix: Change to: 'The rent is good. The flat has a big room.' (The review word 'house' still appears in the vocab list.)

issues.description: The gloss for target word 'rent' only covers the noun ('money you pay...'), but the dialogue's first use is the verb 'rented' ('I've just rented a flat'). A learner checking the gloss at that point cannot map it to the sentence.
issues.suggested_fix: Gloss both uses simply: 'to pay money every month to live in a flat or house; also, the money you pay'.

issues.description: The gloss for 'house' ('a place where people live') is too broad: a flat, a hotel or a tent are also places where people live.
issues.suggested_fix: Change to: 'a building where one person or a family lives'.

issues.description: The gloss for 'room' ('a part of a house with walls') is vague and excludes flats; almost every part of a house 'has walls'.
issues.suggested_fix: Change to: 'a part of a house or flat with its own walls and door'.

issues.description: 'Have you ever just moved to a new home?' combines 'ever' (any time in your life) with 'just' (a moment ago), which native speakers would not say together.
issues.suggested_fix: Use 'Have you ever moved to a new home?' or 'Have you just moved to a new home?'.

qa_report.summary: A clean, level-appropriate micro-dialogue: 'just' and 'already' with the present perfect are both modelled correctly and the grammar note is accurate. The one real problem is a consistency slip in s1l3, where the rented 'flat' becomes 'the house'. The glosses are serviceable but the target word 'rent' is only glossed as a noun although it first appears as a verb, and the 'house' and 'room' glosses are imprecise. Fixable with the suggested edits.
